clue.text: Be involved in a risky action, ruinous to the litigant?

definitions.text: Be involved in a risky action
definitions.meaning: to invite calamity by taking a dangerous step
playfully, a catastrophe suffered in a law court

explanation.surface: A warning to someone about to sue: the lawsuit could ruin them.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to risk calamity; the question mark flags the punning second reading, a calamity in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to invite calamity, and a lost lawsuit is literally a calamity at the courthouse.

clue.text: Rise above plain, up-river

parts.note: plain, meaning open and obvious, is overt

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the river's name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Something climbing higher than the flat land beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To tower over something is to rise higher than it.

clue.text: Wind up with a lively dance?

definitions.meaning: to draw in a fishing line by turning a spool
a brisk Scottish or Irish folk dance

explanation.surface: Finishing an evening off with a spirited dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler winds in line on one; a Scottish country dance of quick steps shares the name.

clue.text: Handsome, and in a hurry

definitions.meaning: stylish and attractive in appearance
rushing along quickly

explanation.surface: A good-looking person rushing somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakish, attractive man is described with this word, which also means rushing hastily.

clue.text: Gibbons wildly wailing

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of the word Gibbons are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Apes in the forest screeching uncontrollably.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying noisily with gulping breaths is a kind of lamenting.

clue.text: Slight drawl

definitions.meaning: an insult or snub
to speak with words run together indistinctly

explanation.surface: A faint, lazy way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a disparaging remark and indistinct, run-together speech.

clue.text: Include in a show of affection

definitions.meaning: to take in or encompass
a hug

explanation.surface: Being welcomed into a group with warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass or adopt something, and also a hug given out of love.

clue.text: Virtually directed to the whole camping

parts.note: something directed to a person is meant for them
the whole means every part, all
people camping are sleeping under canvas, in tents

explanation.surface: Instructions sent to everyone on a camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is short for the idiom ending 'and purposes', meaning in practice or practically.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in effect or practically, which is what 'virtually' says.

clue.text: Britney spears diverted nonconformists

indicators.note: diverted means turned from their course, so the letters of the pop star's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pop star's fame distracting members of a strict church.
explanation.walkthrough: Britney Spears is an American pop singer; her full name is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Scottish-rooted Protestant church were classed as dissenters from the Church of England.

clue.text: Cover removers in action at the start of the cricket match

definitions.meaning: tools for taking lids off jars or tins

definitions.text: in action at the start of the cricket match
definitions.meaning: the two batters who begin a team's innings

explanation.surface: Groundstaff pulling the covers off as a cricket match begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the first two batters to go in are named for beginning the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin and bottle tools take off lids, and in cricket the first pair of batsmen begin the innings.

clue.text: Cry from a whale

definitions.meaning: to weep noisily
the fat layer of a marine mammal

explanation.surface: A whale making a mournful call.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep noisily, and also the thick fat of sea mammals rendered into oil.

clue.text: Performs after John

definitions.meaning: does or plays a role
the New Testament book that follows the Gospel of John

explanation.surface: Someone taking the stage once John has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays a part or does things; also the biblical book recording the apostles' deeds, placed straight after John's Gospel.

clue.text: A wee drop in the bar

definitions.meaning: a tiny liquid measure, one sixtieth of a fluid drachm
a half note found in a bar of music

explanation.surface: Ordering just a small dram at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is a bar of music.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecaries' unit of liquid roughly a drop, and a musical half-note filling part of a bar.

clue.text: Returns to bridge and dozes off

indicators.note: returns means the word for crossing over is turned back to front

parts.note: to bridge a gap is to span it

explanation.surface: A card player who goes back to the bridge table and nods off.
explanation.definitionFit: Short sleeps; dropping off for brief rests.

clue.text: Boy, it is rising — and falling!

definitions.text: Boy, it is rising — and falling!

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the pieces are read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: An exclamation at something going up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the sea's twice-daily rise and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's regular ebb and flow makes it rise and fall each day.

clue.text: Church without many clergy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the church letters surround the other piece

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: A church with few priests to serve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests collectively are referred to by the fabric of their garments, as in 'a man of the cloth'.

clue.text: Friend back on the football side — a real flier

indicators.note: back means the word for friend is reversed

parts.note: a friend is a pal
a wing is a flank of a football pitch

explanation.surface: A mate returning to play out wide for a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a fast winger, but the definition means an actual bird, the peewit.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, a crested plover, is a bird and so genuinely takes to the air.

clue.text: It's high in theatrical circles

parts.note: theatre seating is arranged in tiers called circles; the topmost tier, sometimes called the gods, sits highest of all

explanation.surface: Something valued among the fashionable theatre set.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost seating tier in a theatre sits above the dress and upper circles.

clue.text: Game and its objective

parts.note: the sport is named for its aim, putting the ball through the raised hoop and its mesh

explanation.surface: A sport described together with its goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played mostly by women, whose name describes shooting the ball into a mesh ring.

clue.text: Street winding round one Italian city

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters go around the other piece
winding means the letters of street twist into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A twisty road encircling a city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding' rearranges STREET to TRESTE, and 'round' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic port in the north-east of Italy, near Slovenia.

clue.text: Newspaper articles a number wrongly erased

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are set down in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some figure mistakenly deleted from newspaper copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials expressing a paper's opinion are called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Prompt service for TV personalities

parts.note: prompt here means a cue that feeds presenters their script, not quick service

explanation.surface: Quick, efficient attention given to television celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' reads as 'fast', but it means a reminder of words to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A device scrolling a script beside the camera lens so presenters can read their lines.

clue.text: Valid commercials about suits

indicators.note: about means the advert word is placed around the other piece

parts.note: commercials are adverts, ads
a valid claim is just, well founded

explanation.surface: Lawful advertising campaigns about men's tailoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' reads as clothing, but it is a verb: adapts to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to adapt something so it fits a purpose.

clue.text: Trumpet group touring round port of Brazil

indicators.note: touring round means the group word goes around the port's name

parts.note: a clan is a family group
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A band on tour visiting a Brazilian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval shrill-toned brass instrument, used for rousing calls.

clue.text: Girl providing feed-back

indicators.note: back means the word for eating is written backwards

parts.note: to feed is to dine

explanation.surface: A girl offering her views in response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feed-back' looks like one word, response, but splits into the verb and the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the author Blyton.

clue.text: You may play it but don't let little Josephine

parts.note: to forbid, not allow, is to ban
Jo is a short form of the name Josephine

explanation.surface: Permission to play, but not for young Josephine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument with a round drum-like body, plucked or strummed.

clue.text: Silver wrapped up in note for priests

indicators.note: wrapped up in means the metal's symbol sits inside the note

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver tied up in a banknote meant for clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zoroastrian priestly caste of ancient Persia, whose name is also given to the wise men of the Nativity.

clue.text: It's kept in cellars

parts.note: a cellar is also a small table dish for seasoning, not just a basement

explanation.surface: Something stored down in the basement, like wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cellars' suggests wine stores, but the word also means small table dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Table seasoning is held in small dishes or shakers called cellars.

clue.text: Transport will be up at eleven

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A promise that the car will arrive at eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab carries passengers, a form of hired conveyance.

clue.text: Note to say one is willing

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to say is to state

explanation.surface: A message announcing someone's readiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' puns on having made a will: a person who dies having made one is so described.
explanation.definitionFit: Having made a valid will, so the person has literally 'willed' their estate.

clue.text: It's not a change of position

definitions.text: It's not a change of position

parts.words: It's not a change of position
parts.note: a post or assigned place is a position, and staying put there means no movement

explanation.surface: A remark that something is not a move to a new place.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or appointed place is a position, and the related adjective means not moving.

clue.text: Legal proceedings for the small-minded?

definitions.meaning: former magistrates' courts dealing with minor offences
humorously, meetings for petty, small-minded people

explanation.surface: Court hearings intended for narrow-minded folk.
explanation.walkthrough: These were the old English magistrates' courts for minor cases; the second reading is a joke on 'petty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old English lay magistrates' courts for minor cases; 'petty' also means mean-spirited.
